description: Independent environmental reading assessment draft with ten newly authored questions and evidence references; content sign-off pending

questions.q: What made the festival organisers look for a different system?
choices: They wanted to stop all concerts.
The previous events left too many plastic cups.
The food sellers asked for fewer visitors.
There were no volunteers to help.
questions.explanation: The opening explains that discarded cups and late cleaning led to a change in the festival.

questions.q: What happens when someone brings a borrowed cup back?
choices: They receive a concert ticket.
They can keep a new bottle.
They must pay a second deposit.
They get the deposit money back.
questions.explanation: The cup deposit is returned to a visitor who brings the cup back.

questions.q: What problem were the extra signs and return desk intended to reduce?
choices: The number of food sellers.
The price of drinking water.
Long queues and confusion about returns.
The amount of music during the concert.
questions.explanation: Volunteers added signs and a second return desk in response to concerns about waiting.

questions.q: Why was picking up cups attractive to some children?
choices: They could collect the deposit money.
They were given free concert tickets.
They had to do it for school.
They wanted to open their own desk.
questions.explanation: Children returned abandoned cups and kept the deposits as pocket money.

questions.q: Which type of rubbish was still a problem at the festival?
choices: Only broken glass.
Music posters near the stage.
Food wrappers left on the grass.
Metal cups borrowed from stalls.
questions.explanation: The new cup system did not prevent food wrappers from being left behind.

questions.q: How did the number of rubbish bags change from last year?
choices: It fell from forty to twenty-six.
It increased from twenty-six to forty.
It remained exactly the same.
It fell from forty to four.
questions.explanation: The cleaners filled forty bags last year and twenty-six this year.

questions.q: Why do the organisers want to involve food sellers next year?
choices: They want to sell more drinks.
They still need to reduce packaging waste.
They plan to end the festival.
They want customers to pay higher deposits.
questions.explanation: The final paragraph says organisers will ask food sellers to use less packaging.

questions.q: What shows that the new system did not solve every problem?
choices: Visitors stopped drinking water.
The cups were too expensive to borrow.
Nobody used the return desks.
Some cups disappeared and food wrappers remained.
questions.explanation: The text notes missing cups and remaining food rubbish despite the improvement.

questions.q: What would probably happen if the festival removed its return desk?
choices: The number of concerts would increase.
Visitors would need more food wrappers.
Borrowed cups could be harder to return.
The grass would immediately be cleaner.
questions.explanation: A return point is needed for visitors to give back borrowed cups and reclaim the deposit.

questions.q: Which conclusion best fits the organisers' plans?
choices: One useful change can be followed by further improvements.
The festival should return to disposable cups.
The problem is solved and no more work is needed.
The festival should stop serving food.
questions.explanation: The organisers see progress in reducing cups but plan further measures against other waste.
